name: CryoAtlas
alternateName: CryoAtlas: A Large Curated Dataset and Unified Benchmark for Cryo-EM Atomic Model Building
description: CryoAtlas v1.0 pairs experimental cryo-EM density maps with deposited atomic structures and protein sequences from EMDB/PDB records available up to March 2026. The fixed release has 17,809 entries: 16,657 training and 1,152 test, of which 618 form the common benchmark. The benchmark resource package contains five baseline result/prediction sets, two released ModelAngelo CNN retraining result/prediction sets, and ten example entries. The 618 benchmark targets and ten examples are subsets/views of the fixed split, not additional entries. RecordSets provide typed indexes and released metrics; FileSets identify native scientific payloads within all 70 training/test archives and the resource archive.
citeAs: Mingrui Li, Minzhang Li, Weichen Qin, Yufan Xie, Zhangzhi Xiong, Sixian Shen, Jiakai Zhang, Yuan Pei, and Jingyi Yu. CryoAtlas: A Large Curated Dataset and Unified Benchmark for Cryo-EM Atomic Model Building. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations & Datasets Track. https://openreview.net/forum?id=qHJrv65ncA

rai:dataLimitations: The modeling and benchmark tasks focus on protein chains. Deposited coordinate files may retain additional molecular components; the release is not a nucleotide-modeling benchmark.

Entries require a usable experimental map, deposited atomic model, protein sequence and quality screening. Deposited coordinates and metadata can still contain errors; curation does not establish atomic correctness in every region.

The 618-target comparison subset depends on overlap/length eligibility and successful method outputs, and may underrepresent large or computationally difficult assemblies. The full fixed test pool has 1,152 entries.

A map is treated as a static target. Whole-structure metrics do not exhaustively characterize heterogeneous conformations or functionally important local regions. Generated predictions require validation against experimental density before biological interpretation.
Clinical decision-making and treating model predictions as experimentally validated structures are not established uses.
rai:dataBiases: Coverage follows EMDB/PDB deposition and the availability of paired maps, coordinates and protein sequences, not a balanced sample of biological structures.
Resolution-dependent quality filtering favors entries with strong map support and can reduce coverage of lower-resolution experimental maps.

The common benchmark has method-completion and computational-resource selection effects. Compare stratified results and report training-data overlap instead of interpreting aggregate scores as universal generalization.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No newly collected human-subject, clinical or person-level health records are included. Macromolecular sequences and organism metadata describe scientific structures rather than identifiable participants.
Original deposited CIF metadata can retain publicly available depositor names or contact information. These source attribution fields are inherited from public PDB records.
rai:dataUseCases: Research on protein atomic model building from experimental cryo-EM density maps and sequences; development and testing on the fixed train/test split.
Reproducible comparison of structural accuracy, experimental map agreement and stereochemical quality using complementary released raw/composite metrics.

Analysis by resolution, sequence length, chain count and training-sequence similarity. Metadata indexes and example previews support retrieval and inspection; they are not separate training/evaluation populations.

The benchmark characterizes modeling behavior under its published eligibility, input and tool assumptions. Fairness guarantees, clinical validity and general nucleotide modeling have not been established.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The intended benefit is more reproducible structural-biology research and evaluation. Potential harms include over-reliance on plausible but incorrect generated structures, misleading downstream biological conclusions and general misuse of structural-modeling tools. Retained source accessions, fixed splits, file hashes, complementary measurements and explicit limitations support verification; predictions should be checked against experimental density.
rai:dataCollection: Paired public EMDB maps, PDB coordinates and protein sequences from records available up to March 2026 were assembled and curated. The experimental dataset has 17,809 fixed map-model-sequence entries. Model-generated CIF predictions and evaluation outputs are included separately in the benchmark resource package.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Experimental density maps and accession metadata originate from EMDB; deposited atomic structures and sequences originate from PDB. Model predictions are outputs of ModelAngelo, CryoAtom, EMProt, E3-CryoFold, AlphaFold 3 and two ModelAngelo CNN retraining conditions. These outputs are labeled by method/condition and are not experimental reference coordinates.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Entries without paired usable structures or protein sequences were excluded. Unmodeled residues are represented in the aligned/trimmed FASTA representations rather than filled with invented atomic coordinates. The complete fixed test pool remains available beyond the 618-target common comparison subset.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The documented curation protocol checks map-model coordinate agreement, performs realignment where needed, aligns sequences to modeled chains and supplies terminal-trimmed sequence representations.
Q-score-based and unmodeled-density screening retained 17,809 of the 21,229 eligible paired candidates. Reported resolutions and split membership are retained in the published metadata.
MMseqs2-based sequence clustering and complex-level grouping define the fixed 16,657-entry training and 1,152-entry test split. The benchmark is the common 618-target eligible comparison subset.
Dataset files are packaged by complete EMD entries. Dataset catalogs use the PDB identifiers of the packaged structures; per-file inventories and archive SHA-256 values describe the published bytes.

The image previews are independently scaled maximum-intensity projections of ten existing maps along stored array axes. They are display aids, not new experimental densities or quantitative quality labels.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Map/structure coordinate alignment, sequence alignment/trimming, quality screening, fixed splitting, benchmark selection and release packaging are documented transformations. Experimental map/CIF/FASTA payloads are kept distinct from model-generated prediction files. Catalog and normalized result views do not recompute or rescale published measurements.
rai:dataImputationProtocol: No experimental map voxels or reference atomic coordinates are imputed as new ground truth. Generated model predictions are separate benchmark outputs; unresolved reference sequence regions remain unmodeled.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scientific attribution and deposited coordinates are inherited from EMDB/PDB. Split membership, curation annotations, sequence-similarity measurements and modeling metrics are software-derived. No crowdsourced labeling or newly recruited human annotators were used.

The synthetic component consists of the released prediction CIFs from the named modeling methods and CNN retraining conditions. This metadata does not rerun those models or introduce new predictions. Methods and conditions are identified by folder/table columns; the official reference and retraining result sets are separate.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: CryoAtlas v1.0 is a fixed public snapshot hosted on Hugging Face. Data-file URLs in this Croissant are pinned to repository commit 0779e539e03d62a238eb77427586f9261d3e52c7. Archive hashes, split lists and file inventories define the snapshot. The authors maintain the project website and release documentation. Corrections or additions should be documented as a subsequent revision/version with updated metadata and checksums; fixed split changes require a new version.
